claims.claim: packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts: migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot() now skips the move when the destination path already exists, so an existing destination always wins and neither copy is overwritten or deleted.
Colliding legacy source files are left byte-identical in the agent root, and unrelated legacy sessions in the same pass still migrate into sessions/<encoded-cwd>/.

The regression exercises the real production module (loaded with read-only .prale-eval/subject.mjs across the real fs boundary); it exits zero on the repaired source and fails with an AssertionError on the original fault (missing existsSync(newPath) guard), as shown by the temporary negative control.

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root on Node v24.14.0 with the repaired source: exit 0, 8 assertions passed (destination bytes preserved, colliding legacy source preserved byte-for-byte, no duplicate/replacement artifact, unrelated session still migrated, agent-root listing stable, plus idempotency checks across a second migration pass). Negative control: removing only the `if (existsSync(newPath)) continue;` guard from migrations.ts made the same command exit 1 with `AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal` on the existing-destination bytes (renameSync clobbered the destination and consumed the source); the fix was then restored and the run passed again. The script uses only node: builtins plus the read-only subject.mjs helper, writes fixtures under a mkdtemp directory inside .prale-eval and removes it in a finally block, so no dependencies or network are needed. Limitation: the repository has no node_modules installed, so the package's vitest/tsc suites could not be run; verification relied on the dependency-free standalone regression above.
